_about.what: The shape of one state object in src/content/facts/motorcycle-endorsement-facts.json, with 'what' and 'why' standing in for the 'value' and 'source' of a real fact. Not read by any code.
_about.why: One place that says what each field is for, how we prefer to fill it, and every value a constrained field is allowed to take. Zod will enforce the shape later; this explains it, which Zod never will.
_about.purpose: These facts feed auto-generated quick-facts content whose job is to give a rider the headline answer and send them to the primary source for the detail. Every value must be honest and traceable to a document we hold. It does not have to carry every edge case — copy hedges and links out, and a fact that tries to be exhaustive stops being quick. Record the headline answer; put a genuinely load-bearing exception in meta.note and leave the rest to the source.
_about.factContract: Every fact is a { value, source } pair. 'source' is a key into motorcycle-endorsement-sources.json. A fact is verified if and only if it has a source: source null means not researched, and a source present with value null means checked and there is no single honest answer for this state.
_about.valueTypes: number | string | boolean | [min, max]. A range is exactly two numbers, ascending, in the same unit — used where the honest answer varies by county or provider.
_about.newValues: A constrained field that needs a value not listed here stays null and becomes an end-of-run question. Never invent a vocabulary entry mid-run.

displayOnSite.what: Boolean, not a { value, source } fact. Whether a reader may be linked to this state.
displayOnSite.why: False still builds every page at its real URL so work in progress is viewable, but the cert hub omits the state and all its pages carry noindex. A new state starts false and is published by a separate deliberate edit. The cert-level displayOnSite in site-config.json trumps it.

dateVerified.what: Date every fact in this state object was last verified, as YYYY-MM-DD.
dateVerified.why: The visible trust signal on the state page, and what the 21-day revalidation sweep reads. Bumped only when the whole state was re-checked in one pass — a partial pass leaves it alone, or the date starts vouching for facts nobody looked at.

agencyCode.what: Short agency abbreviation as it appears in body copy — FLHSMV, GA DDS.
agencyCode.why: Lives here rather than in states.json because the agency is cert-family-specific: the same agency serves motorcycle and CDL, but hunter ed would be a different one.

agencyName.what: The agency's full name, spelled out.
agencyName.why: Used on first mention and in structured data; agencyCode carries every mention after.

localTerm.what: What this state actually calls the credential — Florida 'motorcycle endorsement', Georgia 'Class M license'.
localTerm.why: The national term is simply wrong in some states. The cert's name is the default and this overrides it, so copy can use the phrase a rider will recognize.

note.what: Internal only. Bare facts about this state that no field can hold.
note.why: For us, not for readers. Facts only — no caveats, no rationale, no explanation of why a field is null, nothing too minor to matter. If it needs a sentence of justification, it is not a note.

stateDetails.what: User-facing prose explaining this state's quirks on its own page. Null until written.
stateDetails.why: The piece that lets every other field stay cookie-cutter while each state page still earns its own SEO.

examType.what: Whose knowledge exam a rider in this state actually sits, and therefore which document the rest of this block describes.
examType.why:
Deliberately separate from criteria.courseType, because the two diverge: Georgia's course is the MSF Basic RiderCourse but its exam is DDS's own, so a question written from MSF's handbook is not what a Georgian will be tested on. Recording only the course type hid that. This field is also what stops the rest of the exam block being ambiguous — questionCount means nothing until you know whose test is being counted.

THIS IS THE FIELD applies_to RESOLVES AGAINST, not courseType. A question is scoped by what a rider is tested on, not by what they were taught, because being tested on it is the entire reason the question exists. The two fields share one vocabulary, so a bare token would be ambiguous if both were live — only this one is.

values.MSFBRC: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation Basic RiderCourse end-of-course knowledge test. The state administers no motorcycle knowledge exam of its own.
values.MNS2011: A knowledge test set by a provider approved against the 2011 Model National Standards. The state mandates that a test exist but not its form, so it varies by school and no single count or score is honest.
values.GA: Georgia DDS's own Knowledge Exam, administered by the agency.
values.CA: California DMV's own motorcycle knowledge test, administered by the agency. Distinct from the CMSP course's written evaluation, which is a different exam that happens to share a passing score.
values.NY: New York DMV's own motorcycle knowledge test, administered by the agency. The test that issues the class M learner permit, which New York requires before the license.
values._naming: Same convention as courseType: an exam belonging to exactly one state takes that state's code, and only exams spanning states get a broad name. A state code here means content that travels nowhere else.

examName.what: What the agency actually calls this exam, in the agency's own capitalization — Georgia's 'Motorcycle Knowledge Exam'. Null where the documents only ever describe it generically.
examName.why: Same job as meta.agencyName: it lets the page name the thing the way a rider will see it named. It also removes the reason to enumerate one display string per state — a state-specific examType builds its label from this plus agencyCode, so adding a state that runs its own exam costs no copy. Null is a researched answer, not a gap: 'we read the document and it just says knowledge test' is what makes the generic phrasing correct rather than lazy. Verify the capitalization, since a lowercase description is exactly the signal that the value should be null.

examAdministration.what: Who actually runs the knowledge exam named by examType — the issuing agency at its own offices, or the required course.
examAdministration.why:
The time limit question has no numeric answer in most states, and this is the honest one: nobody publishes a duration for an exam a course instructor paces by hand. It exists so the quick-facts time limit row can say something true instead of 'Not published' four times, and it is what lets one sentence be right for Florida and Texas without being wrong for Georgia and California.

A SOURCED NULL MEANS THE STATE HAS NO KNOWLEDGE EXAM AT ALL, which is this field's deviation from the usual contract — site-config's hasExam is per cert, so a per-state absence has nowhere else to live. The cost is that 'there is an exam and we could not tell who runs it' has no expression here; that was accepted, because the administrator is the easiest fact about a test to establish. Never cite this to another fact: who administers an exam says nothing about its format.

values.agency: The credential issuer administers it, at its own service centers. Georgia and California. Neither publishes a duration — both publish a closing-time buffer instead, which is a scheduling rule and never a time limit.
values.course: The required course administers it and the state administers nothing of its own. Florida and Texas. MSF's handbook says only 'Follow RiderCoach instructions to complete the test', and TDLR requires a knowledge examination without setting one parameter of it.

courseWaivesAgencyExam.what: Whether finishing the training course waives the agency's knowledge exam, so a rider who takes the course never sits it.
courseWaivesAgencyExam.why:
Only asked where examAdministration is `agency`; where the course already IS the exam there is nothing to waive, and a sourced null says so. It exists because the skills half of this question was already recorded and the knowledge half was not: ridingSkillsTest told us Georgia and California both let the course waive the riding test, and nothing anywhere said that Georgia's waives the written exam too while California's does not. The lede consequently told Georgians to sit an exam their course exempts them from.

DELIBERATELY INDEPENDENT OF ridingSkillsTest. The two booleans cross freely — waives both (Georgia), waives skills only (California), waives knowledge only (a state we have not met yet) — and collapsing them into one 'what the course waives' token would have to be torn apart the first time a state took the fourth corner.

values.true: Course completion exempts a rider from the agency's knowledge exam. Georgia, whose 90-day GMSP waiver covers the written and on-cycle tests both.
values.false: The agency's knowledge exam is required whether or not a rider takes the course. California, whose DL 389 certificate waives the skills test alone.

questionCount.what: Number of questions on the knowledge exam named by examType.
questionCount.why: Where a state administers no test of its own, this describes the knowledge test inside the required course — examType records which, and meta.note carries the detail. Without examType this field silently implied a DMV exam that does not exist.

timeLimitMinutes.what: Minutes allowed for the knowledge exam.
timeLimitMinutes.why:
Frequently unpublished. When an agency genuinely states no limit, the honest record is value null with a source attached, not an unresearched null. A source is earned by reading the document where a duration WOULD appear and finding none — an agency's own testing page, not a licensing overview.

Unpublished is not the same as untimed, and the field must never be filled by inference: DC's DMV publishes a 60-minute motorcycle limit and fails you at it, so silence elsewhere is silence, not proof of an absence. Where this is null, examAdministration is what the quick-facts row falls back to.

passingScorePercent.what: Percentage of questions that must be correct to pass.
passingScorePercent.why: Cannot express a per-section gate on its own — see isExamSectioned before recording one for a split exam.

isExamSectioned.what: Whether the knowledge exam is split into separately scored sections.
isExamSectioned.why: A holding field, deliberately. Georgia's exam is two 20-question sections each needing 15 correct, which questionCount 40 plus passingScorePercent 75 flattens into a score that passes a rider who failed. This flags the case so exam mode never scores one wrong; the real section model gets designed once several states' segmentation is known rather than guessed now. When true, meta.note records the segmentation as bare facts.

values.true: Scored in two or more parts, each with its own gate.
values.false: One undivided test with a single passing score.

practiceExam.what: The agency's own practice test, valued as the short name the state page calls it by. A RESOURCE FACT: the source is not a document backing a claim, it is the practice test itself, and the page links straight to it.
practiceExam.why: Same shape as criteria.findCourse, and for the same reason — the destination is already a registry entry, so a second copy of the URL in the value would be a drift vector and the audit sweep already checks the link is live. The value is a title rather than a bare true because an adjacent official test can be worth offering when it is labelled honestly: Georgia's is the CAR test, offered because the Class M knowledge exam is sectioned Road Rules and Road Signs exactly as it is and the signs half is common to both, and titled 'General Road Rules Practice Test' so no rider reads it as motorcycle-specific. That overlap is a reason to link it and never evidence about the exam — nothing about a state's real exam may be cited to this source. A third-party practice site is not a source under any circumstances.

values.<title>: Their name for it, shortened but not re-worded, where they publish one; ours where they don't. Title Case, since it is link text inside 'the official {agencyCode} …'. Honest about scope before it is short.
values.null: No official practice test worth offering was found. This is a checked answer, not a gap — the field carries no sourced-null form, because the source and the resource are the same thing.

dmvCost.what: Total the rider pays the agency for the credential, in USD.
dmvCost.why: A single number where the state charges one, a [min, max] range where it varies by county or office. The registry note records what the figure is composed of, since a total assembled from three line items is not checkable without it.

classCost.what: What the rider course costs, in USD.
classCost.why: Usually a range, because providers set their own tuition. Where the number is a survey of rates published by the providers an agency directory lists — rather than a figure the agency prints — the registry note must say so, or the next revalidation hunts for a line that was never there.

minAge.what: Youngest age at which the credential itself can be obtained.
minAge.why: The credential, not the learner permit. A state offering a permit at 16 and the license at 17 records 17; the permit age is a meta.note fact.

minLicense.what: What a rider must already hold before pursuing this credential.
minLicense.why: Constrained rather than free text so the state page can branch on it.

values.Learners: A learner or instruction permit is required first.
values.Drivers: A full, already-issued driver license is required first. Deliberately generic — states name the same credential differently (Florida Class E, Georgia Class C), and localTerm is where state naming lives.

transferOutOfStateEndorsement.what: Whose existing motorcycle credential this state accepts in place of retesting.
transferOutOfStateEndorsement.why: Constrained so the UI can branch. Note the shape is already strained: a value naming one specific state does not scale, and a third exclusion pattern is the signal that this field wants to become a list rather than a token.

values.all: Accepts a valid motorcycle credential from every other US jurisdiction.
values.none: Accepts no out-of-state credential in place of retesting. Every applicant tests in-state regardless of what they hold elsewhere — California is the case.
values.non-Alabama: Accepts every other US jurisdiction outright. An Alabama credential is accepted only when presented with an MSF Basic RiderCourse completion card — the token names the exception, and copy carries the condition.

courseRequired.what: Whether this state requires rider training of anyone at all, before it issues the credential.
courseRequired.why:
THE ONE FIELD THAT OWNS THE REQUIREMENT CLAIM. Nothing else in the tree — no display string, no template sentence, no panel label — may assert that a course is required, because that is exactly how the lede came to tell Georgians and Californians their optional course was mandatory. The four MVP states gave three different answers to the most consequential question a rider asks, which is why this cannot be a constant in prose.

Expect it to look redundant beside courseType and classCost. It is not: those describe a course that may or may not be compulsory, and neither can say which.

values.true: Somebody must take a course. Whether that is everybody or only riders under an age is what courseRequiredUnderAge narrows. Florida and Texas require it of every applicant; California only of riders under 21.
values.false: Nobody is required to take a course, though one is normally still available and usually the easier route. Georgia, where the GMSP course and testing directly at a DDS service center are two independent paths to the same license.

courseRequiredUnderAge.what: The age below which courseRequired applies. Null means the answer it gives is not narrowed by age.
courseRequiredUnderAge.why:
An integer rather than a token because the values are ordinal and a new cutoff should cost no vocabulary entry — 18 and 21 are both common, and 50 states will supply others.

NULL HERE IS NOT A SENTINEL FOR 'EVERYONE'. It means courseRequired stands unqualified: with true, required of all ages; with false, required of nobody. A single integer was weighed for the whole job and could not carry it — 'everyone' is not an age, and spelling it as a magic number or as null would make an unresearched state render as 'required for everyone', which is worse than the bug this replaced. The intro template reads it as a placeholder rather than a gate, so the age-bounded sentence drops itself wherever this is null.
courseRequiredUnderAge.example: 21 in California: the CMSP course is mandatory under 21 and optional at 21 and older.

courseType.what: The rider-training curriculum this state's course is built on. What the rider was TAUGHT — exam.examType is what they are TESTED on, and the two do not always match.
courseType.why: Descriptive, not load-bearing: it drives display and tells authoring what training a rider actually received, but applies_to resolves against exam.examType instead — scoping follows what a rider is tested on. Verify it rather than assuming: California runs CMSP, several states run programs that are MSF-derived but distinct. Sharing a curriculum is weaker evidence than it looks — two states on the same course type can still teach different figures in their own manuals, so it does not by itself make content portable.

values.MNS2011: Any curriculum the state approved against the 2011 Model National Standards for Entry-Level Motorcycle Rider Training (USDOT/NHTSA). Used where the state regulates to a standard instead of naming a curriculum, so several conformant curricula — MSF's among them — may be in use at once. Deliberately not MSFBRC: a rider's school may have taught something else.
values.CA: California's own curriculum, delivered by the CMSP under CHP contract. Naming convention: a curriculum belonging to exactly one state takes that state's code, and only curricula spanning states get a broad name like MSFBRC. Keeps question assignment legible — a broad token means a group worth authoring for, a state code means content that travels nowhere else.

findCourse.what: How a rider finds and books a course.
findCourse.why: Decides which call to action the state page shows. Lives in criteria despite not being a criterion, so all the fact objects stay grouped.

values.stateLocator: The agency publishes a directory of independent providers and the rider contacts one directly.
values.stateProgram: The agency runs a single booking portal covering all courses.

ridingSkillsTest.what: Who administers the on-motorcycle riding evaluation, and whether the required course gets a rider out of it.
ridingSkillsTest.why: Informational only — LanternCert prepares nobody for a riding test, and this exists so the state page does not imply the knowledge exam is the last hurdle. Constrained rather than free text because the state page branches on it, including branching to silence: 'course' emits no sentence at all. The values split on the WAIVER, not on who administers the test, because the waiver is the only part a rider acts on — two states can both run an agency test and still owe different answers to 'will I actually have to sit it'. Verify the waiver conditions rather than the test's existence: nearly every state has one of these, and the conditions are what differ.

values.course: The state administers no riding test of its own; the required course's own on-cycle evaluation is the whole thing, and the agency records the result. Florida is the case — the FRTP Sponsor submits the result electronically and the endorsement is added. Note this is INFERRED from absence: no FLHSMV page states the agency administers no riding test.
values.agencyWaivable: The agency administers a riding test, and completing the required course waives it for anyone. Georgia and California.
values.agencyUnlessLicensed: The agency administers a riding test, waived only for adults who already hold a full driver license in the state, and never waivable for a minor. Texas is the case: the course is required of everyone but does not on its own waive the skills test.

requirementType.what: What kind of machine triggers the requirement for this credential.
requirementType.why: Constrained because it decides who the page is even for — a rider on a 49cc scooter needs a different answer than one on a 650.

values.50ccUp: Required for any motorcycle above 50cc; 50cc and under is treated as a moped.
values.all: Required at every engine size, with no moped exemption. California is the case: a moped or motorized bicycle needs a Class M2 and a motorcycle needs an M1, so there is no unlicensed tier at all.
values.30mphUp: Required for any motorcycle able to exceed 30 mph, with no displacement test at all. New York is the case: it classes a limited use motorcycle by maximum performance speed, so a class A (over 30 mph) needs a Class M while a class B or C (30 mph and under) rides on an ordinary Class D. Never substitute 50ccUp here - a 49cc scooter that does 35 mph is a class A and does need the license.

renewalYears.what: Whole years the credential lasts before it must be renewed. 0 means it does not expire on its own.
renewalYears.why: An integer rather than a token, so a new term needs no vocabulary entry and the value can be compared, sorted and rendered by the same number-plus-unit path every other figure uses. 0 carries 'never' because null already means 'not researched' and the two are different claims — a state that never expires the credential is a verified fact, not a gap.

additionalResources.what: An array of registry keys for user-facing links that no fact already cites.
additionalResources.why: The 'Verified against' list is derived from the source fields, so this holds only what would otherwise never appear on the page. Never repeat a key already used as a source — the two render as separate lists and a duplicate shows up twice.
